Entry Literacy and Oral Memory Literacy was more common among the nobility, the Citadel, and the town guilds, with the vast majority still relying on memory, oral messages, and ballads to preserve the past. Things written down appear reliable, but may not be more honest; people who cannot write also know how to remember a debt, a road and a journey. Whether it is valid depends on who can grant the rights, collect the consideration, and actually make the judgment come to fruition in the event of default.
